prerequisites: No prior course knowledge is assumed.

learning_outcomes.text: Have knowledge and understanding of the fundamentals of business organization and management, the concept of a company, its institutional and legal framework.
Be aware of the multidisciplinary context of industrial engineering, applying knowledge of mathematics, statistics, economics, and other scientific fields to the analysis of business situations.
Be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to the analysis of process and methods engineering.
Have an understanding of different methods and the ability to use them for the analysis of business situations.
Be able to select and use appropriate methods for business management.
Be aware of the implications of engineering practice in business management.
Function effectively both individually and as part of a team.
Demonstrate awareness of the responsibility of engineering practice, its social and environmental impact, and commitment to professional ethics, responsibility, and standards of engineering practice.
Demonstrate awareness of business and project management practices, as well as risk management and control, and understand their limitations.
Knowledge and understanding of the scientific and mathematical principles underlying their branch of engineering.
Awareness of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to the analysis of product, process, and methods engineering.
Understanding of different methods and the ability to use them.
The ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools, and methods.
Awareness of all implications of engineering practice.
Function effectively both individually and as part of a team.
Demonstrate awareness of the responsibility of engineering practice, its social and environmental impact, and commitment to professional ethics, responsibility, and standards of engineering practice.
Demonstrate awareness of business and project management practices, as well as risk management and control, and understand their limitations.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects involving knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated by elaborating and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge and abilities to organize and manage projects. Knowing the organizational structure and functions of a project office.
Adequate knowledge of the concept of a company, its institutional and legal framework. Organization and management of companies.
Knowledge and ability to analyze and evaluate the social and environmental impact of technical solutions, and to apply environmental and sustainability technologies.
Ability to establish good interpersonal communication and to work in multidisciplinary and international teams.

syllabus_topics: Concept and nature of the company. Company and entrepreneur.
Types of companies and legal forms.
The role of engineering and the engineer in business management.
Strategic analysis. Company objectives and strategies.
Value creation. Competitive strategy and business models.
Financial Management: Economic-Financial Analysis of the Company
Financing decisions. Internal and external sources of financing.
The management function. Leadership and motivation.
Innovation and Business Growth. Technology-Based Companies (EBTs)
Innovation management. Strategies for technology protection and exploitation.
teaching_methods: Exercise and case solving by students
Class discussion of assignments, cases, and supplementary readings
assessment_rules: The final exam accounts for 60% of the grade, with a minimum score of 4 out of 10 required to pass the course. Continuous assessment accounts for 40% of the grade.
